latin: Quilibet numerus planus aequilaterus animam symbolizat.
translation: Every plane equilateral number symbolizes the soul.
translation_note: 'Numerus planus aequilaterus' is Farmer's own gloss, 'square number' (farmer1998:17101).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch9, from Latin at farmer1998:17022
doctrine: Farmer connects this thesis's numerological premise to his own broader argument that the square number 900 (30×30) carried, within the numerological tradition Pico draws on, a symbolism of the soul roused to self-return through poetic frenzy — part of Farmer's own explanation for why Pico's text comprises exactly 900 theses (farmer1998:17101).
context: Farmer's cross-reference network links the thesis to 1.6 from Albert the Great on the separated soul's innate species (farmer1998:17022).
historiography: Allen (2017) cites this thesis together with 25.14, from Pico's Opera Omnia (Basel, 1572, p. 79), in a discussion of Ficino's Timaeus commentary on point, line, plane and solid as stages mediating between center and circumference, associating such figures with souls and minds (allen2017:2687).
not_established: Farmer's further cross-reference 'Cf. 521' (a cumulative thesis number) is not resolved to a section.number id in the material consulted.
